Feed the result to the existing SLSQP as the start with radii set to 0.4 of the nearest-neighbour distance divided by 2. This differs from the earlier penalty replacement because it keeps SLSQP as the final solver and uses a fixed distance target.
backlog.title: Two-scale overlap penalty with smooth continuation

backlog.spec: Build a random symmetric matrix A of size n by n from the seeded rng, take its eigenvector of the largest eigenvalue for each of the two coordinates, and map the two eigenvectors to the unit square by a rank-based rescaling to get centres. Use the resulting layout only as the start for a random half of the non-guided restarts, with radii set to the small INIT_RADIUS. This gives a structured but random initialisation with different spatial correlations from the uniform, Halton and jittered-grid starts that were already tried.
backlog.title: Spectral clearance-matrix start

backlog.spec: Rescale the decision vector so that every centre coordinate and every radius has unit typical size: write centres as 0.5 + 0.5*u with u in [-1, 1], and radii as r = 0.1*s. Run SLSQP on the scaled variables u and s, then unscale before the repair. The variable scaling improves the step length and tolerance behaviour of SLSQP for n = 32 without changing the optimum. Keep the constraint function and the repair unchanged, and keep the time loop unchanged.
backlog.title: Mixed-precision SLSQP chain with a scaled step

backlog.spec: For one fixed slice of the time budget (about 40 percent), call scipy.optimize.differential_evolution on the 2n centre coordinates in [0,1]. The objective is minus the sum of radii from a fast deterministic construction: for each candidate set of centres, compute radii greedily by sorting all pairs and boundary limits, giving each circle the largest radius that fits. Use popsize=10, maxiter set so the call stops at the slice limit, and seed=the solve seed. Take the best DE centres, run _solve_once with them as init and zero jitter, then repair. Keep the rest of the random-restart loop unchanged.
backlog.title: Differential evolution over centres with SLSQP polish

backlog.spec: Replace one slice of the random restarts with scipy.optimize.dual_annealing over the 2n centre coordinates bounded in [0,1]. Decode each candidate with a greedy pass: radius of circle i is min of its wall distances and half its distance to every already-placed circle minus the neighbour's radius, processed in a fixed order. The objective is minus that sum. Run with maxiter limited by the time slice and seed=seed. Pass the best decoded centres to SLSQP as init (with zero jitter), repair, and keep if better than the incumbent.
backlog.title: Dual annealing over centres with a fast greedy radius decoder

backlog.spec: Maintain a swarm of 20 particles whose positions are the 2n centre vectors in [0,1]^(2n), with velocities initialised from the seed rng. Each particle's fitness is the greedy-decoded sum of radii (largest radius that fits given the earlier circles in index order, bounded by walls). Update velocities with inertia 0.7 and cognitive and social weights 1.5, clipping positions to [0,1]. Every 200 evaluations, take the swarm best, run _solve_once from its centres with zero jitter, repair, and update the incumbent. Stop at the slice limit of CPU time.
backlog.title: Particle swarm over centres with SLSQP polish of the swarm best

backlog.spec: Encode a packing as a random-key vector of length n whose argsort gives the insertion order. Decode by placing circles in that order, each at the sampled point of a fixed 60x60 grid that maximises its feasible radius given earlier circles (the radius is the min of wall distance and distance to placed circles minus their radii). Run a generational GA for a slice of the budget: tournament selection of size 3, uniform crossover of keys, Gaussian key mutation with sd 0.05, elitism of 2. Polish the best decoded packing with _solve_once using its centres and zero jitter, repair, and compare to the incumbent.
backlog.title: Random-key genetic algorithm over greedy insertion order

backlog.spec: Split the random-restart budget across 4 islands, each with its own rng drawn from seed plus island index and a local elite of size 3. Islands alternate in rounds: in each round each island performs 5 restarts (uniform random starts for the first two rounds, then starts from a random elite of its own or of the ring neighbour with probability 0.5 using the existing jitter). After every round, the best elite of each island is copied to the next island in the ring, replacing its worst elite if better. The global best is the incumbent that is returned. This is a batch-level change; the SLSQP solve and repair are unchanged.
backlog.title: Island model with ring migration of elite packings

backlog.spec: For each non-guided restart, start from uniform random centres and radii 0.05. Run 400 steps of overlap-energy Langevin dynamics: energy is the sum of squared positive overlaps of pairs, squared wall violations and a term -sum(r). Take an explicit gradient step with step size 1e-3 plus Gaussian noise of scale sqrt(2 T dt), where the temperature T decays geometrically from 0.05 to 1e-5 over the steps. Vectorise with numpy broadcasting. Use the final configuration as the SLSQP start, then run the existing _solve_once from it and repair.
backlog.title: Langevin dynamics on the overlap energy before SLSQP

backlog.spec: Replace the pairwise greedy shrink in _repair with a single global rescale. Compute for every pair the ratio s_ij = d_ij / (r_i + r_j) and for every wall the ratio of the radius to the available clearance. Let s be the minimum over all pair and wall ratios that is below 1. Multiply all radii by s, then take the wall-limited radii again and keep SHRINK. Repeat until no pair ratio is below 1 - 1e-12, with at most 50 passes. Because the scaling is uniform, rattlers keep their relative size and the total loss is typically smaller than the pairwise method. Everything else is unchanged.
backlog.title: Global-scale repair instead of pairwise shrinking

backlog.spec: Solve each restart in the box [0, L] x [0, L] where L is a free variable appended to the SLSQP vector, with the objective minus the sum of radii and an added constraint that L is at least 1 minus a small slack. All wall constraints use L instead of 1. After SLSQP, set the centres to c divided by L and the radii to r divided by L, which produces a packing in the unit square with the same ratio of sum to side. Apply the repair and keep the best. This lets the optimiser trade box shape against circle sizes at no cost to the validity check.
backlog.title: Scaled-box solve with a free side length then rescale

backlog.spec: Keep the random restarts for the first 60 percent of the time fraction. In the next 25 percent, run guided restarts from the incumbent with jitter amplitude that halves every 10 restarts. For the final 15 percent, take the top 3 distinct repaired packings and run one _solve_once from each with MAX_ITER raised to 1000 and zero jitter, then repair. The incumbent is the best repaired result. The only change is the time split and the final long solve; the restart logic is otherwise unchanged.
backlog.title: Three-level schedule that spends the last 20 percent on one long SLSQP

backlog.spec: For each pair of restarts, draw one uniform random start U and use both U and its reflection about the box centre (1 - U) as starts for two SLSQP solves with the same rng state for the jitter. Keep the better repaired result of the two, and carry both into the incumbent comparison. Use the rng seeded from the solve seed so that the pair structure is reproducible. This doubles the chance that a basin with the mirrored layout is found from the same cost in starts and tests whether the starting distribution, not the solver, is limiting.
backlog.title: Antithetic pairs of random restarts with shared seeds

backlog.spec: For a random subset of non-guided restarts, build the initial centres from k horizontal shelves, with k drawn uniformly from {3,4,5,6} using the seed rng. Split the n circles across shelves with random counts that sum to n (each at least 1). Place each shelf's centres evenly along x at its height, with the shelf heights equally spaced in [0.1, 0.9], then add N(0, 0.02) jitter. Set the initial radii to a fraction of the shelf spacing, and pass the layout to the existing SLSQP solve. Everything else (repair, selection, guided logic) stays unchanged.
backlog.title: Shelf-structured starting layout

backlog.spec: Replace the overlap-shrinking loop in _repair with a spreading step that keeps the radii fixed. For up to 200 sweeps, loop over all overlapping pairs (r_i + r_j - d_ij > 0) and push each centre apart along the line of centres by half the overlap, weighted by r_j/(r_i+r_j) for circle i and the complement for circle j. After each sweep, clip the centres to [r_i, 1-r_i]. Stop when no overlap exceeds 1e-12. Shrink only the residual overlapping radii with the existing pairwise rule. Keep the final SHRINK margin.
backlog.title: Centre-spreading repair instead of pairwise shrinking

backlog.spec: Track a velocity vector v over the incumbent centres. Each time the incumbent improves, set v = (new_centres - old_centres) plus 0.5 times the previous v. For guided restarts, start from incumbent + v + small jitter (N(0, 0.005)) rather than from the incumbent alone, so the search extrapolates along the direction of recent improvements. Use the same guided-probability schedule as the current script. Reset v to zero whenever a guided restart fails to beat the incumbent for three consecutive tries.
backlog.title: Heavy-ball momentum across guided restarts

backlog.spec: For half of the non-guided restarts, place four circles at the four corners of the square (centres at (r0, r0), (1-r0, r0), (r0, 1-r0), (1-r0, 1-r0) with r0 = 0.1) and sample the remaining n-4 centres uniformly in [INIT_LOW, 1-INIT_LOW]. The corner circles start with radius INIT_RADIUS, and SLSQP then frees all variables as usual. The corner circles are not frozen, so the solver can move them. This biases starts toward the boundary-contact structure that good packings tend to have.
backlog.title: Corner-pinned random starts

backlog.spec: After the free-radius SLSQP solve, run up to 6 alternating block steps. In each step, freeze the y-coordinates and radii and solve SLSQP over the x-coordinates with the non-overlap and wall constraints; then freeze x and radii and solve over y. Each block is a smaller, better-conditioned problem. Stop early when the sum of radii changes by less than 1e-7. Apply the repair step to the final packing as before.
backlog.title: Alternating x-only and y-only block solves

backlog.spec: Adapt the guided-restart jitter scale sigma with the one-fifth success rule. Start sigma at 0.03. After each guided restart, if it improves the incumbent multiply sigma by 1.2, otherwise multiply it by 0.9^(1/4). Clamp sigma to [1e-3, 0.1]. Keep the existing guided probability and switch time. The jitter used by each guided restart is N(0, sigma) per coordinate, so the step size adapts to the local landscape without a fixed schedule.
backlog.title: One-fifth success rule for guided jitter

backlog.spec: Keep the last 4 repaired packings in a small buffer. When choosing the parent for a guided restart, run a single-elimination tournament among the buffer entries, using the repaired radius sum as the score with ties broken by the rng. The winner is the parent. The incumbent is still the global best for the final return value. This is a selection-rule change only, with no change to how starts or solves are generated.
backlog.title: Tournament selection among recent solves

backlog.spec: Before each guided restart, apply a random element of the 8-element symmetry group of the square to the incumbent centres (the identity, the three rotations, and the four reflections), chosen by the seed rng. Then apply the usual isotropic jitter and the SLSQP solve. The flip does not change the packing's quality, but it moves the jitter relative to the box walls and so explores different wall-contact patterns. Keep the switch time and guided probability unchanged.
backlog.title: Random 90-degree symmetry flip of the incumbent before guided jitter

backlog.spec: After each repaired SLSQP solve, run two extra SLSQP passes from the solver output. Before each extra pass, perturb the centres by a random displacement drawn uniformly on a disc of radius 0.5 times the median radius of the current packing, then clip to the box. Keep the best repaired packing across the three passes as the restart's result. This is a small iterated-local-search step inside each restart and does not touch the global restart loop.
backlog.title: Iterated local SLSQP with a small random kick per solve

backlog.spec: Replace the fixed TIME_FRACTION = 0.8 with a budget-aware stop: keep launching restarts until the time used reaches 0.9 of time_limit, but cap any single restart's SLSQP maxiter at a value set from the remaining time (maxiter = max(30, min(MAX_ITER, remaining_seconds divided by the average time per iteration measured so far))). This spends the last part of the budget on a shorter final solve instead of leaving it unused. The harness limit of 45 s CPU is respected by keeping the total under 0.9 times the 30 s limit.
backlog.title: Use all remaining CPU budget with a final restart-length cap

backlog.spec: Replace the 4n wall inequality constraints in the SLSQP stage with a smooth bijection. Optimise unconstrained variables u (2n) and set centres c = r + (1 - 2r) * sigmoid(u), where r is the current radius vector, or use a fixed margin of 0.5*INIT_RADIUS. Radii keep the bound r >= 0 as a box constraint. The pairwise non-overlap constraints stay as they are. After the solve, map back to centres, then run the usual clip and repair. Gradients go through the sigmoid by the chain rule, or are left to SLSQP finite differences. This changes the constraint geometry and conditioning rather than the search distribution.
backlog.title: Sigmoid box reparametrisation that removes wall constraints

backlog.spec: For a fraction of non-guided restarts (say half), build the starting centres by maximising the minimum pairwise distance of n points in [0,1]^2. Introduce an epigraph variable t, maximise t subject to |c_i - c_j|^2 >= t for all pairs and 0 <= c <= 1, and solve with SLSQP from a random start. Use the resulting centres as the initial configuration for the usual radius-and-centre SLSQP solve, with initial radii set to half the minimum pairwise distance divided by 2. This is a deterministic dispersion objective, unlike the Riesz energy start that was already tried.
backlog.title: Max-min dispersion start via epigraph SLSQP

backlog.spec: Maintain an elite set of the best 5 repaired packings. Each restart draws a start by picking an elite packing and perturbing each centre with an independent Gaussian whose per-circle standard deviation is fitted from the elite spread (the sample standard deviation of each circle's position across elites, floored at 0.01). Every 10 restarts, refit the elite set and the per-circle standard deviations from the top 5 results seen so far, which is the cross-entropy update. Seed all draws from rng. Unlike the single-incumbent guided jitter, this learns a per-circle variance from the population.
backlog.title: Cross-entropy method over start-configuration distribution

backlog.spec: For non-guided restarts, draw n centres by Poisson-disk (dart-throwing) sampling with a random minimum distance drawn from the seed rng, inside [0.05, 0.95]^2. Compute scipy.spatial.Delaunay on the points. Set each radius to 0.5 times the shortest edge incident to that circle, clipped by the wall distance, so that the start is almost feasible. Then run the usual SLSQP solve and repair. This tests a start whose contact graph is a triangulation, which differs from the random uniform and hexagonal starts already tried.
backlog.title: Delaunay-edge radius start from a Poisson-disk sample

backlog.spec: After each SLSQP solve, read the active constraint multipliers from the solver result if available, or estimate them by a least-squares fit of the gradient of the objective onto the active pair-constraint gradients. Keep the pairwise constraints with a multiplier above 1e-6 plus every pair whose gap is below 0.05, and pass only these to the next solve on the same restart. Do a single full-constraint check after the solve and add back any violated pair before repair. This uses the dual information to shrink the constraint set, which is a different criterion from the start-position pair restriction that was already tried.
backlog.title: Lagrange-multiplier-guided constraint pruning

backlog.spec: For guided restarts, instead of jittering the incumbent in place, draw a fresh uniform random configuration of n points and match it to the incumbent centres with scipy.optimize.linear_sum_assignment on the squared-distance cost matrix. Permute the random points so that each incumbent circle receives its nearest unused random point, then add a small jitter of 0.01 to each matched point. The assignment step decouples the circle identities from the current labels, so the restart samples a new layout that keeps the incumbent's rough density. Seed everything from rng.
backlog.title: Hungarian-matched guided starts

backlog.spec: After the random-restart loop, find rigid clusters of the best packing. Build the contact graph with gap below 1e-6, and take connected components with at least 3 contacts. For each cluster, treat its circles as a rigid body with a shared translation and rotation, reducing the variables to 3 per cluster plus the free rattlers. Solve the reduced SLSQP problem with the overlap constraints only between clusters and boundary contacts, then expand back to full coordinates and repair. Accept the result only if the sum of radii improves. This is an architectural reduction of the variable count, not a random move.
backlog.title: Rigid-cluster reduction of the incumbent

backlog.spec: Replace the greedy pairwise shrink in _repair with a feasibility restoration based on Dykstra's alternating projection. Each constraint set is one of: the non-overlap set for a pair (project the two centres apart along their line until the distance equals the sum of radii), or the box set for each circle (clip centre to [r, 1-r] and radius to [0, min wall distance]). Cycle over the constraint sets for up to 200 sweeps in a random order from rng. Stop when the maximum violation is below 1e-12, then apply a final pure shrink of 1e-10 to guarantee the harness tolerance. The point is that centres move as well as radii, so less total radius is lost than in pairwise shrinking.

memo: Helped: only slot 1, guided restarts from the best packing in the second half of the budget (-2.9365, delta -0.0112). It is a single run and the noise sd is about 0.0034, so it is unconfirmed. Nearly all of the other ~70 slots were within noise or worse. That covers new initialisations (2, 6, 9, 18, 29, 34, 38, 40, 50), solver swaps (4, 5, 24), post-polish steps (16, 28, 31, 33), population schemes (20, 23, 37) and guided-restart variants (14, 39, 49, 58, 63, 65, 67, 75). Slots 11, 24, 62 and 68 were far worse, and slot 35 crashed. Near misses on the baseline: 21 and 27 (-2.9396), 6 (-2.9386) and 17 (-2.9380). Slots 13 and 30 reached -2.9370 on top of slot 1, which is not clearly better. Next: 1) Replicate slot 1 to fix the baseline. 2) Stack 21 or 27 on slot 1, then 6 and 17, one at a time, with replicates. 3) Tune the guided fraction. 4) Avoid more initialisation, post-polish, symmetry or population ideas.
